parts.text:
A broom is being used to sweep a rough horizontal floor. The handle of the broom makes a constant angle of $40^\circ$ with the horizontal, as shown in Figure 1. The broom head is modelled as a particle of mass $0.5\,\mathrm{kg}$ and the handle of the broom is modelled as a light rod. The coefficient of friction between the broom head and the floor is $\frac{1}{4}$. The broom head is pushed along the floor in a straight line at constant speed. Find the magnitude of the force that is being applied along the handle of the broom to the broom head.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
$F=\frac{1}{4}R$ B1: use of $F=\mu R$ with $\mu=\frac{1}{4}$ seen or implied
$P\cos40=F$ B1: resolve horizontally. Accept $F\cos40^\circ=F_{max}$. Not $F\cos40^\circ=F$
Resolve vertically M1: all terms required, and dimensionally correct. $P\neq R$. Condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion
$P\sin40+0.5g=R$ A1: correct unsimplified equation
$P(4\cos40-\sin40)=0.5g$ DM1: substitute for $R$ and solve for $P$. Requires zero acceleration. Dependent on previous M1
$P=2.0$ (N) or $2.02$ (N) A1: 2 or 3 sf only
SC if F opposes their P, 6/6 available. If P and F inconsistent max score available B1B0 M1A1follow their diagram DM1A0
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Condone if P acting in the wrong direction but see SC below

questions.stem: A beam $AB$ has mass $100\,\mathrm{kg}$ and length $8\,\mathrm{m}$. The beam is held in equilibrium in a horizontal position by two vertical ropes attached to the beam at $C$ and $D$, where $AC=0.5\,\mathrm{m}$ and $BD=0.5\,\mathrm{m}$. A gymnast of mass $M\,\mathrm{kg}$ stands on the beam at the point $P$, where $AP=2\,\mathrm{m}$, as shown in Figure 2. The beam remains horizontal and in equilibrium. The tension in the rope attached to the beam at $D$ is $637\,\mathrm{N}$. The gymnast is modelled as a particle, the beam as a uniform rod and the ropes as light inextensible strings.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find
(i) the value of $M$,
(ii) the tension in the rope attached to the beam at $C$.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
Moments equation M1: all terms required, dimensionally correct. Condone sign errors
M(C): $Mg\times1.5+100g\times3.5=637\times7$ A1: correct unsimplified equation
[or M(A): $2Mg+400g=\frac{1}{2}T+7.5\times637$; M(P): $1.5T+100g\times2=637\times5.5$]
Resolve vertically or a second moments equation M1: all terms required, dimensionally correct. Condone sign errors
$(\uparrow)$, $T+637=Mg+100g$ A1ft: correct unsimplified equation in $M$ or their $M$, $T$ or their $T$
(i) $M=70$ A1: $69.99...=70$ is A0 (from 9.81)
(ii) $T=1000\,\mathrm{N}$ or $1030\,\mathrm{N}$ A1: not $1029$, not $105g$
They need to form two independent equations. M1A1 for first equation seen, M1A1ft for the second equation (ft on any result from the first eqn), A1 for M, A1 for T.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) State how you have used the fact that the beam is modelled as a rod.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: B1: assumed that the beam remains straight. Not flexible B1, Does not bend B1. Extra irrelevant (e.g. centre of mass at midpoint) B0

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The gymnast at $P$ now gets off the beam and is replaced by two gymnasts. One gymnast, of mass $60\,\mathrm{kg}$, stands on the beam at $P$ and the other gymnast, of mass $48\,\mathrm{kg}$, stands on the beam at $X$, where $AX=x$ metres. The beam remains horizontal and in equilibrium but the tensions in the two ropes are now equal. The two gymnasts are modelled as particles.
(c) Find the value of $x$.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
$T+T=60g+100g+48g$ M1: resolve vertically. Need all terms. Equal Ts. Condone sign errors
$(T=104g$ or $1019.2\,\mathrm{N})$ A1: correct unsimplified equation
Moments equation M1: all terms required, dimensionally correct. Not using T from (a). Condone sign errors
M(C): $60g\times1.5+100g\times3.5+48g\times(x-0.5)=T\times7$ A1: correct unsimplified equation
[or M(A): $60g\times2+100g\times4+48gx=0.5T+7.5T$; M(B): $0.5T+7.5T=48g(8-x)+4\times100g+6\times60g$; M(D): $100g\times3.5+48g(7.5-x)+60g\times5.5-7T=0$]
Solve for x DM1: solve for their x. Dependent on both preceding M marks
$x=6.5$ (m) A1
Watch out for a "correct" answer from working that ignores the 100g. As above, M1A1 for two independent equations, then DM1A1 for solving.

questions.stem:
A railway truck of mass $500\,\mathrm{kg}$ is pushed up a straight track by a railway engine of mass $2000\,\mathrm{kg}$. The track is inclined to the horizontal at an angle $\theta$, where $\sin\theta=\frac{1}{14}$, as shown in Figure 3. The engine produces a constant driving force of magnitude $3050\,\mathrm{N}$. The truck experiences a constant resistance to motion of magnitude $100\,\mathrm{N}$ and the engine experiences a constant resistance to motion of magnitude $200\,\mathrm{N}$. The engine and the truck are connected by a coupling which is modelled as a light rod that is parallel to the track.
Find
(i) the acceleration of the system,
(ii) the magnitude of the force exerted on the truck by the coupling.

parts.mark_scheme:
(i) Equation of motion for the system M1: all terms required, dimensionally correct. Condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion
$3050-300-2500g\sin\theta=2500a$ A1A1: unsimplified equation with at most one error. Correct unsimplified equation. NB a sign error on the 300 or a sign error on $2500g\sin\theta$ counts as 2 errors (to be consistent with the penalty if they did this in 2 separate equations)
$a=0.4$ (m s$^{-2}$) A1: not $\frac{2}{5}$ (follows 9.8)

(ii) Equation of motion for the truck M1: all terms required, dimensionally correct. Condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion
$T-100-500g\sin\theta=500a$ A1A1: unsimplified equation with at most one error. Consistent sign for T. Correct unsimplified equation (in a or their a)
$T=650$ (N) A1: must be positive

(ii) alt: Equation of motion for the engine M1: all terms required, dimensionally correct. Condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion
$3050-200-2000g\sin\theta-T=2000a$ A1A1: unsimplified equation with at most one error. Condone negative T. Correct unsimplified equation
$T=650$ (N) A1: must be positive

(i) and (ii) can be solved together by forming the two separate equations of motion and solving using simultaneous equations. M1A1A1 for each equation and A1A1 as above.
If the 100 N and the 200 N are associated with the wrong vehicles, treat this as a MR. This error gives them T=750

questions.stem: Two forces $\mathbf{F}_1$ and $\mathbf{F}_2$ act on a particle. The resultant of the two forces is $\mathbf{R}$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Given that $\mathbf{R}$ has the same direction as the vector $(3\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j})$,
(a) find the size of the angle between $\mathbf{R}$ and the vector $\mathbf{j}$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
$\tan\theta=\frac{2}{3}$ M1: use trig to find a relevant angle ($56.3^\circ$, $33.7^\circ$)
Angle is $\theta+90^\circ=123.69^\circ$ A1: $124^\circ$ or better ($2.16$ radians)

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
$\mathbf{F}_1+\mathbf{F}_2=(a\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j})+(-4\mathbf{i}+b\mathbf{j})(=k(3\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}))$ M1: resultant force seen or implied: must be the sum, NOT the difference. As a column vector or in i/j form

$\frac{a-4}{3+b}=\frac{3}{-2}$ A1: correct unsimplified equation
$0=2a+3b+1$ Given answer A1: obtain given answer from correct working - need to see evidence

questions.stem:
[In this question $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are horizontal unit vectors due east and due north respectively and position vectors are given relative to a fixed origin $O$.]
A ship $A$ is moving with constant velocity $(2\mathbf{i}-14\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{km\,h}^{-1}$. At 2pm the position vector of ship $A$ is $(8\mathbf{i}+7\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{km}$.
A ship $B$ is moving with constant velocity $(12\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{km\,h}^{-1}$. At 2pm the position vector of ship $B$ is $(\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{km}$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show that at time $t$ hours after 2pm,
$\overrightarrow{BA}=[(7-10t)\mathbf{i}+(5-10t)\mathbf{j}]\,\mathrm{km}$
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
Use of $r=r_0+vt$ M1: at least once. Must be adding, not subtracting
$r_A=(8\mathbf{i}+7\mathbf{j})+t(2\mathbf{i}-14\mathbf{j})$ A1: $r_A$ correct $\begin{pmatrix}8+2t\\7-14t\end{pmatrix}$
$r_B=(\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j})+t(12\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j})$ A1: $r_B$ correct $\begin{pmatrix}1+12t\\2-4t\end{pmatrix}$
$\overrightarrow{BA}=(8\mathbf{i}+7\mathbf{j})+t(2\mathbf{i}-14\mathbf{j})-[(\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j})+t(12\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j})]$ M1: need to see an indication of method as leading to a given answer
$=(7-10t)\mathbf{i}+(5-10t)\mathbf{j}$ A1: obtain given answer from correct working

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Hence find the length of time for which the ships are within $2\,\mathrm{km}$ of each other.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
Use of Pythagoras to equate distance to 2 km M1
$(7-10t)^2+(5-10t)^2=2^2$ A1: correct unsimplified equation in t
Form 3 term quadratic in t M1
$20t^2-24t+7=0$
$(10t-7)(2t-1)=0$ DM1: solve for t. Dependent on the preceding M1. Must see working if using an incorrect quadratic
$t=\frac{7}{10}$ or $\frac{1}{2}$ A1
Time $=\frac{7}{10}-\frac{1}{2}$ DM1: correct method to find the time interval. Dependent on the preceding M1
$=\frac{2}{10}$ h (12 min) A1

questions.stem: Three particles, $P$, $Q$ and $R$, have masses $4m$, $3m$ and $2m$ respectively. Particles $P$ and $Q$ are connected by a light inextensible string that passes over a smooth light fixed pulley. Particle $R$ is attached to particle $Q$. The system is held at rest with the string taut and the hanging parts of the string vertical, as shown in Figure 4. The system is released from rest.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find
(i) the acceleration of particle $P$,
(ii) the tension in the string.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
Equation of motion for P or for Q&R M1: all terms required and dimensionally correct. Condone sign errors. If m missing throughout, mark as a misread
$5mg-T=5ma$ or $T-4mg=4ma$ A1: one correct unsimplified equation
Second equation of motion M1: condone if second equation is for the whole system
$5mg-T=5ma$
$T-4mg=4ma$ A1: a second correct unsimplified equation
